title: I Enforced the Parking-Permit Color on the Dean's Unmarked SUV

parts.text: I ticketed lot C at 8:11 a.m. in a student-staff vest. A black SUV sat in a faculty-green space with no permit. The dean got out and said everyone knows the car. I was twenty-three, parking services, holding a printer that does not know cars. Policy is color on glass. I photographed the empty corner and printed a citation. He told me to void it. I asked him to call the supervisor while I continued down the row. At 8:16 he parked the citation on my windshield as a joke, which is how supervisors find things.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The citation is on my windshield and the SUV is still in faculty-green.

social.description: Student vest, empty glass, a joke on my windshield. Would you have voided it?

parts.text: The supervisor logged both. The SUV got a real permit after a real payment. My windshield got clean. Everyone knows is not a color. I still ticket lot C. The printer still does not know cars. The dean waves now with glass that matches. Jokes that relocate citations become exhibits. Green means green. I keep the vest on until the row is done.

social.video_title: The joke became an exhibit — Part 2/2
social.description: Paid permit, clean glass, lot C continues. Was fame a sticker?
